ontology.purpose: Build a tactical-doctrine ontology of land-force offensive, defensive, and enabling operations as defined in ADP 3-90. The ontology must let a planning or wargaming system answer, for any named tactical concept, what it is, what purpose it serves, what its characteristics and defining criteria are, how it is classified (type, form, variation), which echelon or formation typically executes it, and how it relates to other concepts (e.g., which forms of maneuver belong to the offense, which control measures apply to a defensive technique). It is intended to ground automated mission-analysis, COA-development, and doctrinal-term normalization tools.
ontology.scope: IN SCOPE: the art and science of tactics; tactical fundamentals and the tactical level of warfare; common tactical concepts (areas of operations, control measures, forms of contact, combat formations, echelons and their roles); the offense — purposes, characteristics, types of offensive operations (movement to contact, attack, exploitation, pursuit), forms of maneuver, attack variations, organization of forces; the defense — purposes, characteristics, types of defensive operations (area, mobile, retrograde) and their forms and techniques; enabling operations (reconnaissance, security, troop movement, relief in place, passage of lines); doctrinal definitions, and graphic-control-measure names that the document defines or references. OUT OF SCOPE: unit-specific TTPs, weapon-system data, staff-process step details covered by other publications, and any content not stated in this document.
